Currently

I am developing EXD-Net, an independent computational project examining how stored representations respond to perturbations in attractor-based memory systems.

The current implementation uses Hopfield networks to evaluate pattern convergence, energy trajectories, and retrieval stability under increasing input corruption. Ongoing work explores how destabilization, reweighting, and representational drift may extend the model from pattern recovery to memory updating and adaptive learning.

The broader question motivating this project is how internal representations form and change in systems while preserving sufficient structure to support continuity across time.
